claims.text: Refractory high-entropy and compositionally complex alloys are candidates for fusion plasma-facing structural applications.
A hierarchical network of coherent nanoprecipitates governs high-temperature plastic strain and toughness in refractory HEAs or CCAs.
A three-dimensional network of deformation-induced twins governs high-temperature plastic strain and toughness in refractory HEAs or CCAs.
The proposed unperturbed initial state is a single-phase solid solution without pre-existing nanoscale features.
A controlled thermomechanical treatment can create stable coherent nanoprecipitates or a twin network in the selected refractory alloy.
Rapid quenching or omission of annealing suppresses coherent nanoprecipitates and deformation twins, producing a homogeneous baseline.
Temperatures of 600–1000 °C are representative of the intended fusion service regime.
In the proposed test regime, dislocation glide dominates while diffusion is active but limited.
The nanoscale features impede dislocation glide and thereby strengthen the alloy.
The nanoscale features increase dislocation storage and strain hardening.
The nanoscale features provide multiple pathways for dislocation transfer.
Progressive strain hardening distributes plastic strain and delays localized plastic instability.
Delayed localization also delays crack initiation or propagation and improves toughness at high temperature.
Relative to the homogeneous baseline, the feature-bearing alloy will have higher high-temperature yield strength.
Relative to the homogeneous baseline, the feature-bearing alloy will have a greater strain-hardening rate and extended uniform elongation at high temperature.
Relative to the homogeneous baseline, the feature-bearing alloy will have enhanced fracture toughness at high temperature.
The mechanism is limited to moderate strain rates and may weaken outside 600–1000 °C or in substantially different alloy chemistries.
The quantitative property improvements depend on nanoscale-feature morphology, alloy chemistry, and processing details.

contradictions.description: The control logic treats rapid quenching as suppressing both precipitates and twins, but the proposed twins are deformation-induced and may instead form during pre-strain or subsequent mechanical testing. Thus the baseline does not necessarily isolate twin presence in the same way that it can suppress annealing-induced precipitation.
